answer: RAM: a memory-hard kernel builds each identity's 4 GB table from its own seed and the domain tag terrace. Verifiers mirror expected entries in unpredictable simultaneous spot checks, rejecting wrong values or replies beyond a deadline calibrated below measured disk latency. Identity-bound tables prevent shared copies; overlapping checks hinder pooling and time-slicing. One honest agent reserves 4 GB; 1,000 fakes require about 4 TB resident concurrently. This linear memory cost discourages mass fakes, not all attacks.
